correctness.rationale: The exact digit-block decomposition proves S(bx)=B S(x) for every integer x. The finite geometric sum computes Fourier factors w_r without singular denominators (n odd). On nonconstant modes, B^2 has eigenvalue -u_r^2; the odd-binomial identity and zeta^{rn}=1 give P(-u_r^2)=0. On constants P(0)=n, hence P(B^2)=J. Applying to the exact transfer and pairing digits of consecutive integers proves all x and residue classes. Exact integer-matrix checks through n=41 and direct original-sum checks at n=3,5,7 corroborate; no finite sample is promoted to infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim resolves two explicit, literature-motivated conjectures simultaneously for all odd composite and prime moduli, gives a uniform structural matrix annihilator and exact cutoff-residue identity, and removes a documented restriction to small moduli. This is not simply another fixed n verification or a re-evaluation of a known coefficient table. It makes no asymptotic or sign claim not established by the proof.
